games.summary: Oregon (3-2) is a 7-point home favorite over Nebraska (5-1), total 51.5, but QB Dante Moore (concussion) is OUT again and Oregon has not named a starter between Dylan Raiola (6/19, 43 yds, 2 INT vs UCLA) and Brock Thomas. Nebraska's defense allows 15.2 ppg; player props are excluded (Ohio ban), so the legs are game, team-total and first-half lines.

ALCS Game 4 makeup after Friday's rainout, Guardians up 2-1: Nick Martinez (3.10 ERA, 1.09 WHIP) for Tampa Bay, and reliever Shawn Armstrong opens a Cleveland bullpen game again. Both bullpens got an extra day of rest.

No. 5 Indiana (6-0, 22-game win streak) hosts No. 4 Ohio State (5-1) at noon on FOX as roughly a 3-3.5 point home underdog with a total of 50.5; SP+ projects a 26-26 tie. Ohio State's injury list has six players out, including starting OT Austin Siereveld (now out, second straight game missed) and RB Ja'Kobi Jackson, plus five questionable players such as RB Isaiah West. Player props are dropped (Ohio bans college player props); the legs cover the side, OSU team total, first half and the game total.

Florida (4-2, two straight losses) is expected to start sophomore Tramell Jones Jr. (first career start) at No. 7 Texas (4-1), with Aaron Philo (shoulder) questionable; reports (On3/Nakos, CBS/Zenitz, Saturday Down South) point to Jones, but there was no official pregame confirmation as of this check. The market already moved toward Texas -11 and a total of 51.

Mississippi State QB Kamario Taylor (turf toe) was downgraded to doubtful and is not expected to play per ESPN's Pete Thamel; freshman Parker 'Billy' Puckett would start, and leading rusher Fluff Bothwell is also doubtful. The market already moved hard on this (LSU -11.5/-14 to -17.5, total 58.5-59.5 to 56), so edges are modest; best lean is the Mississippi State team total under.

SMU (4-1, off a bye, 3-0 at Ford Stadium) hosts Virginia (4-2) with SP+ projecting SMU 30-23 and FPI giving Virginia about 31%, roughly in line with the market's -8.5 to -10 spread and 51.5 total. The clearest angle is SMU's passing offense (Jennings 317.6 yds/g) against a Virginia secondary missing CB Omillio Agard for the season, with both starting safeties doubtful.

No. 6/7 Alabama (5-1) is a -7.5/-8 road favorite at No. 14 Tennessee (5-1) with the total down from about 56.5 to 51; Tennessee starts backup-turned-starter George MacIntyre (Faizon Brandon questionable, shoulder) while Alabama is without WR Ryan Coleman-Williams, C Racin Delgatty and five defenders. Tennessee's defense (15.5 ppg, 4.7 yds/play, 161 pass ypg, nation-leading 25 sacks) against Alabama's leaky pass protection (113th in sacks allowed) is the main matchup.

No. 13 Missouri (5-1) visits No. 9 Ole Miss (4-1) at homecoming. Ole Miss is a 5.5-point favorite, down from 6, with the total at 58.5. Missouri's top-25 defense (16.6 ppg, 78 rush ypg allowed) and SEC-leading rusher Jamal Roberts (828 yds, 138/g) face an Ole Miss run defense that ranks last in the SEC (176 ypg allowed). Both starting QBs are healthy: Simmons was taken off the injury report, and Missouri RB Ahmad Hardy is out. Ohio bans college football player props, so only game, team-total and first-half lines are proposed.

No. 2-3 Notre Dame (6-0, 4-2 ATS) visits No. 8 BYU (5-0 SU and ATS) at night with College GameDay in town. BYU is without RB LJ Martin. ND CB Leonard Moore (concussion) is questionable but practicing, and DT Jason Onye (ankle) is questionable. The market is ND -10.5 at about a coin flip, with the total down from 48.5 to 46.5.

No. 12 UCLA (5-0, 5-0 ATS) hosts Wisconsin (4-1, off a bye) at night in the Rose Bowl, with backup Ty Dieffenbach (Cal Poly transfer, 3/6 for 43 yds in relief) making his first UCLA start because Nico Iamaleava has a leg injury that is expected to end his season. The market has moved toward Wisconsin (spread from 3 to 2.5) and the Under (total from 44.5 to 42.5-43.5), and most Action Network experts back Wisconsin +3.

No. 15 Kentucky (5-1, four straight wins incl. OT upsets of South Carolina and LSU) visits 3-2 Oklahoma, which just beat No. 1 Texas 27-24 on an elite defense (about 238 ypg allowed) but a sputtering offense (10, 14, 13, 27 vs FBS opponents). The market (OU -6.5, total 43.5) looks efficient; the only lean is the Oklahoma team total under 24.5.
